title: Senna Heights: forest views for a family that works from home.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #461 | SENNA HEIGHTS, DAMANSARA DAMAI
excerpt: A new two-tower launch that will be the tallest in Damansara Damai, ringed by forest reserve. Sean drives the morning rush first, then tours a 1,464 sq ft family layout.
takeaways: 780 units on 6.5 acres, all above 1,000 sq ft, with a 100 m pool and a rooftop over the forest.
About RM600 psf: the 1,464 sq ft Type A costs around RM800,000 and has a separate wet kitchen.
One way in and out, an older neighbourhood and rents that don't yet justify it as an investment are the concerns.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Senna Heights is two leasehold towers, 780 units on 6.5 acres with 18 shop lots in front, and will be the tallest building in Damansara Damai. The drop-off sits at the back for privacy, with a lawn, trails and kids' play by the entrance. The deck has a 100 m pool, an elevated gym, a half basketball court and a maze garden, and the rooftop looks over forest reserve on every side.

Each tower has four lifts for 10 units a floor, all facing north or south. Sean tours Type A, a 1,464 sq ft corner unit with three bedrooms, a flexi room and two bathrooms, a separate wet kitchen and yard, and a 6.6 m-wide living and dining area; the flexi room comes without walls, for buyers to enclose. At about RM600 psf, it costs around RM800,000.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: Damansara Damai is tucked between forest reserves and highways including the LDP and NKVE, reached from Jalan Kuala Selangor. A one-way ring road now carries traffic in and out; at the morning rush Sean took about 8 minutes to reach the main traffic light. Damansara Damai MRT station is about 8 minutes' drive, served by a developer shuttle, and runs to TRX without a change of line.

pros: Designed for own stay: a hidden location, residential access kept apart from the shops, a drop-off at the back, 780 units on 6.5 acres all above 1,000 sq ft, a 100 m pool and a rooftop over the forest. The kids' lawn by the entrance greets you every time you come home.

Type A, perhaps the developer's best layout yet: a recessed foyer, a landscape-format living, dining and dry kitchen against a wide balcony, and its first proper wet kitchen behind a partition, with a yard. The flexi room comes open, so buyers add the walls and door themselves, as the sale agreement states.

The developer's track record: a former contractor that keeps its sales gallery on site, with construction nearing podium level. Its completed projects match their show units, cabinets and wardrobes included, and this one is going for GreenRE certification.
cons: One way in and out of Damansara Damai, through the same traffic light onto the highway. The one-way ring road has helped: at the morning rush Sean took about 5 minutes to the McDonald's and 8 to the traffic light, busy but moving. It suits those who work from home.

First impressions: an older area of public housing, low-cost flats and sewage and water treatment plants, though the MRT has brought new projects. Sean prefers being some distance from the station, with a shuttle, and deeper in are attractive landed homes and townhouses.

It stands apart from its older surroundings, whose rents can't justify its price, so it is not a cash-flow investment. In time it may draw owners upgrading from older apartments or downsizing from landed homes.

closing: A strong own-stay choice at about RM600 psf for a family that works from home, if Damansara Damai suits you.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this August 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The developer's team hosted the visit at the on-site sales gallery, and Sean drove the area at the weekday morning rush.
